name: Moped
description: A motor-driven scooter, cycle or similar vehicle on no more than three wheels whose motor produces no more than 1,500 W final output (or 2 gross brake horsepower, or 50 cc) and that can't go faster than 30 mph on a flat surface. An electric two-wheeler over the e-bike limits lands here while it stays within these. Electric bicycles and electric scooters are excluded.

restrictions.rule: No more than three wheels on the ground; pedals aren't required (Nevada Revised Statutes §482.069)
Its motor produces no more than 1,500 W final output, 2 gross brake horsepower or 50 cc (Nevada Revised Statutes §482.069)
Can't go faster than 30 mph on a flat surface with the motor engaged (Nevada Revised Statutes §482.069)
A motor vehicle for licensing, so riders need a driver's license; it isn't a motorcycle, so no motorcycle license or endorsement
Riders and passengers must wear a helmet, plus glasses, goggles or a face shield unless a windscreen meeting DMV standards protects them
Registered once with the DMV after an inspection confirms it's a moped, with a plate distinct from a motorcycle's; the registration lasts until it's sold
Its owner needn't carry the liability insurance required of motor vehicles
On a highway with two or more lanes each way, kept to the far right lane except to turn left
Must have two mirrors and fenders, and the rider must be able to reach the ground with both feet
